channel.title: AI Stupa Translation Project
channel.description: New English translations of texts from the Tibetan Buddhist canon, made by the AI Stupa (provisional, public domain).

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Thoroughly Pacifying All Illnesses" (Toh 1014)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Thoroughly Pacifying All Illnesses," known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Sarvaroga­praśamani Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Pakpa Né Tamché Rabtu Shiwar Jepa Shejawé Sung, is a brief dhāraṇī text that offers a protective incantation for healing a wide range of bodily ailments. Set in Prince Jeta's Grove at Śrāvastī, it opens with the Buddha urging the assembled monks to take…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī That Thoroughly Pacifies Illness (Toh 1015)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī That Thoroughly Pacifies Illness, known in Tibetan as Phakpa Né Rabtu Zhiwar Jepé Zung and probably corresponding to a Sanskrit title along the lines of Ārya Roga Praśamanī Dhāraṇī, is a very brief incantation text devoted to healing. After paying homage to the Three Jewels and to the Buddha under the name Vajra Guru King, it gives a short mantra that invokes the vajra and calls…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Completely Pacifying Fever" (Toh 1016)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Completely Pacifying Fever," known in Sanskrit as the Āryajvarapraśamanināmadhāraṇī and in Tibetan as 'Phags pa rims nad rab tu zhi bar byed pa zhes bya ba'i gzungs, is a short protective scripture meant to relieve those afflicted by fever. It opens at the great charnel ground of Śītavana near Rājagṛha, where a monk asks the Buddha to protect beings tormented by fever…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī for Pacifying Epidemic Disease (Toh 1017)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī for Pacifying Epidemic Disease is a very brief protective incantation preserved in Tibetan translation, and its Sanskrit and Tibetan titles are known chiefly from its closing line, which names it after its purpose of calming epidemic illness. After paying homage to the Three Jewels and to the Buddha Amitābha, the text gives a short mantra that names the person to be protected and…

item.title: The Noble Sūtra That Thoroughly Pacifies Eye Disease (Toh 1018)
item.description: The Noble Sūtra That Thoroughly Pacifies Eye Disease, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Akṣirogapraśamanisūtra and in Tibetan as Phags pa mig nad rab tu zhi bar byed pa'i mdo, is a brief scripture concerned with healing afflictions of the eyes. Set on Vulture Peak Mountain near Rājagṛha, it opens with the great yakṣa general known as the Black One approaching the Buddha and asking how eye diseases…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī That Pacifies the Disease of Smallpox (Toh 1019)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī That Pacifies the Disease of Smallpox is a very brief incantatory text whose title is known here in English. Its Sanskrit and Tibetan titles cannot be determined with confidence from the source at hand. After a simple homage to the Three Jewels, it consists almost entirely of a single dhāraṇī, a Sanskrit spell addressed to the Blessed Mañjuśrī in his youthful form. The spell invokes…

item.title: The Noble Sūtra That Thoroughly Pacifies Hemorrhoids (Toh 1020)
item.description: The Noble Sūtra That Thoroughly Pacifies Hemorrhoids, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Arśapraśamanī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Zhangdrum Raptu Zhiwar Jepé Do, is a short Mahāyāna scripture that offers a healing incantation for relief from this painful affliction. The text opens at Rājagṛha, in the Bamboo Grove, where the Buddha is seated before a great assembly of monks on the full-moon observance…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī for Clearing Away the Illness of Indigestion (Toh 1021)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī for Clearing Away the Illness of Indigestion is a very brief healing incantation, and its Sanskrit and Tibetan titles are not given in the material available here. After paying homage to the Three Jewels and to the Tathāgata called King of the Radiance of Fire, it presents a short mantra and a simple accompanying rite: one recites the mantra over one's hand and then rubs the belly…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī Completely Pacifying All Hostility (Toh 1022)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Completely Pacifying All Hostility" is a very brief incantation text, known in Tibetan as a gzungs, or dhāraṇī. It opens with homage to the Three Jewels and to the Buddha Samantadarśin, the "All-Seeing," and then gives a short mantra. Its instruction is that anyone who recites the mantra seven times while supplicating the bodhisattva Mañjuśrī will find that all people…

item.title: The Dharma Text of the Buddha's Treasury (Toh 123)
item.description: The Dharma Text of the Buddha's Treasury, known in Tibetan as Sangs rgyas kyi mdzod kyi chos kyi yi ge, is a Mahāyāna sūtra that also bears the alternative title The Instruction Given on All Phenomena. Set on Vulture Peak Mountain near Rājagṛha before a great assembly of monks and countless bodhisattvas, it opens with Śāriputra rising from meditation to question the Buddha about his teaching that…

item.title: The Noble Sūtra of Mahālakṣmī (Toh 1005)
item.description: The Noble Sūtra of Mahālakṣmī, known in Sanskrit as the Āryamahālakṣmīsūtra and in Tibetan as Pakpa Pal Chenmö Do, is a brief scripture centered on the goddess of fortune and prosperity, Mahālakṣmī. Set in the pure land of Sukhāvatī, it opens as the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara approaches the Blessed One. The Buddha then turns his attention toward Mahālakṣmī and declares that anyone who knows her…

item.title: The Twelve Names of the Goddess Śrī (Toh 1006)
item.description: The Twelve Names of the Goddess Śrī, known in Tibetan as Pal gyi Lhamo'i Tsen Chunyipa, is a short scripture devoted to Śrī, or Lakṣmī, the great goddess of fortune and prosperity. It opens in the realm of Sukhāvatī, where the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and the great goddess Śrī, herself honored here as a bodhisattva and great being, come before the Blessed One. The Buddha then turns to…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Vasudhārā (Toh 1007)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Vasudhārā, known in Sanskrit as Āryavasudhārānāmadhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Nor gyi Gyün zhejawé Zung, is a short scripture centered on a dhāraṇī, a sacred incantation associated with Vasudhārā, the goddess whose name means "stream of wealth." The text opens at Kauśāmbī, where the Buddha is staying in the Kaṇṭaka forest with a great assembly of monks and…

item.title: The Noble Vidyā-Mantra Called Purifying the Eye (Toh 1008)
item.description: The Noble Vidyā-Mantra Called Purifying the Eye, known in Sanskrit as Āryacakṣurviśodhanī nāma vidyāmantra and in Tibetan as Pakpa Mik Nampar Jongwa Zhejawé Rikngak, is a short scripture centered on a vidyāmantra, a spell of awareness, whose title points to the purification and healing of the eyes. It opens in the classic sutra manner, with the Blessed One staying among the Śākyas, and introduces…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Completely Purifying All Karmic Obscurations" (Toh 1009)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Completely Purifying All Karmic Obscurations, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Sarvakarmāvaraṇaviśodhanī Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Le Kyi Dripa Tamche Nampar Jongwa Shyejawé Zung, is a brief incantation text centered on a single dhāraṇī-mantra. Opening with homage to the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, it presents the mantra and then explains its rite and benefits. Constant…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī-Mantra That Dispels All Obstacles (Toh 1010)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī-Mantra That Dispels All Obstacles, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Sarvāntarasaṃgrāsa Dhāraṇī Mantra and in Tibetan as Pakpa Bardu Chöpa Tamché Selwé Zung Ngak, is a short dhāraṇī text in which the Blessed One addresses the bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi about the protective power of a sacred incantation. The Buddha explains that anyone who upholds, carries, and recites this dhāraṇī-mantra…

item.title: Thorough Purification of Offerings (Toh 1011)
item.description: The Thorough Purification of Offerings, known in Sanskrit as the Dakṣiṇāpariśodhanī and in Tibetan as Yon yongs su sbyong ba, is a brief dhāraṇī text concerned with purifying the offerings that donors make to the religious community. After paying homage to all buddhas and bodhisattvas, to the tathāgata Samantaprabharāja, and to the bodhisattva Mañjuśrīkumārabhūta, it presents a short incantation…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī for Purifying Offerings (Toh 1012)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī for Purifying Offerings, known in Tibetan as Yon yongs su sbyong ba'i gzungs, is a very brief dhāraṇī text that gives a single incantation for purifying offerings, especially gifts received in faith. The dhāraṇī pays homage to the Tathāgata Sumeru Kalparāja, the "King of Aeons like Mount Meru," and then invokes purification with the words kalpe, kalpe, mahākalpe. The text explains…

item.title: Dhāraṇī of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Who Completely Clears Away All Lower Realms, the Arhat, the Perfectly Complete Buddha (Toh 1013)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī of Purifying All Lower Realms, whose Sanskrit title likely corresponds to Sarvadurgatipariśodhana, is a very brief scripture centered on the Tathāgata whose name in Tibetan, Ngensong Tamché Yongsu Selwa, means "He Who Completely Clears Away All Lower Realms." After paying homage to this buddha, the text gives a short mantra-like incantation, or dhāraṇī, that calls for the purification…

item.title: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra of the Great Parinirvāṇa (Toh 120)
item.description: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra of the Great Parinirvāṇa, known in Sanskrit as the Āryamahāparinirvāṇanāmamahāyānasūtra and in Tibetan as Phagpa yongsu nyangen le depa chenpo thekpa chenpo'i do, is a Mahāyāna sūtra set at the very end of the Buddha's life. It opens in the grove of twin sāla trees near Kuśinagara, on the bank of the Hiraṇyavatī River, where the Buddha, surrounded by a vast assembly…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Mother of All Dharmas (Toh 996)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Mother of All Dharmas, known in Sanskrit as the Āryā Sarvadharmamātṛkā Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Chö Thamché Kyi Yum Shejawé Zung, is a short scripture centered on a protective incantation. Set at Śrāvastī, it opens with the Buddha instructing his attendant Ānanda to retain this dhāraṇī, which he describes as having been spoken by all the tathāgatas and as…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called the Mother of the Planets (Toh 997)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called the Mother of the Planets, known in Sanskrit as Āryagrahamātṛkā nāma dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Za Yum Zhejawé Zung, is a dhāraṇī scripture centered on the goddess revered as the Mother of the Planets. It opens in the great city of Aṭakāvatī, where the Buddha sits on a lion throne among bodhisattvas such as Vajrapāṇi. He is praised by a vast assembly of gods, nāgas…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī Called Mother of the Planets (Toh 998)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī Called Mother of the Planets, known in Sanskrit as the Grahamātṛkā Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as gza' rnams kyi yum zhes bya ba'i gzungs, is a dhāraṇī scripture concerned with the planetary and astral forces that were believed to shape human fortune. It opens in the great city of Aḍakavatī, where the Blessed One sits upon the vajra throne. He is praised by gods, nāgas, yakṣas and other…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī of the Eight Goddesses (Toh 999)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī of the Eight Goddesses, known in Sanskrit as the Āryāṣṭadevīdhāraṇī and in Tibetan as 'Phags pa lha mo brgyad kyi gzungs, is a brief incantatory scripture in which the bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaims a powerful dhāraṇī-mantra. The text praises this mantra as a supreme great queen among dhāraṇīs and as the mother of the tathāgatas, a feminine power said to purify all wrongdoing…

item.title: The Hundred and Eight Names of the Venerable Noble Tārā (Toh 1000)
item.description: The Hundred and Eight Names of the Venerable Noble Tārā, known in Sanskrit as the Āryatārābhaṭṭārikānāmāṣṭaśataka and in Tibetan as rje btsun 'phags ma sgrol ma'i mtshan brgya rtsa brgyad pa, is a short devotional text in praise of the female buddha Tārā, renowned as a swift protector and liberator from fear and suffering. After an opening homage, the text is set on Mount Potala, a richly…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī of Noble Tārā (Toh 1001)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī of Noble Tārā, which may be rendered in Sanskrit as Āryatārādhāraṇī and in Tibetan as 'Phags ma sgrol ma'i gzungs, is a very brief incantation text devoted to the female bodhisattva Tārā. After paying homage to the Three Jewels and to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the great compassionate bodhisattva, it presents a single mantra built on Tārā's characteristic syllables, tāre tuttare ture…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī Called "The Vow Made by Noble Tārā Herself" (Toh 1002)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī Called "The Vow Made by Noble Tārā Herself," known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Tārā Svapratijñā Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Pakma Drolma Rang Gi Damchepa Zhejawai Zung, is a short dhāraṇī text devoted to the female bodhisattva Tārā. After an homage to Noble Tārā, it presents her speaking a dhāraṇī-mantra that embodies the vow she herself made, and it extols its power: simply calling it…

item.title: The Noble Great Queen of Vidyā-Mantras Called Jayavatī (Toh 1003)
item.description: The Noble Great Queen of Vidyā-Mantras Called Jayavatī, known in Sanskrit as Āryajayavatīnāmamahāvidyārājā and in Tibetan as Phakma Rikngak kyi Gyalmo Chenmo Gyalwa Chen, is a short scripture centered on a protective incantation personified as the great queen of spells, Jayavatī, "the Victorious One." It opens with the Buddha dwelling on Mount Videha at a time when faithless gods, nāgas, yakṣas…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Jayavatī (Toh 1004)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Jayavatī, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Jayavatī Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Pakpa Gyalwachen, is a short scripture centered on a protective incantation described as a "great queen of spells." It opens on Vulture Peak near Rājagṛha, where the Buddha is staying with a thousand monks, and Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, approaches and asks him to proclaim…

item.title: The Noble Great Queen of Vidyā-Mantras (Toh 985)
item.description: The Noble Great Queen of Vidyā-Mantras, She of the White Parasol Who Arose from the Uṣṇīṣa of All the Tathāgatas, Invincible by Others, She Who Turns Back, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣasitātapatrā Aparājitā Pratyaṅgirā Mahāvidyārājñī, is a scripture centered on the protective goddess Sitātapatrā, the White Parasol. In Tibetan it is known as a text on the great queen of…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī of the Invincible Lady with the White Parasol Who Emerged from the Crown of the Tathāgata (Toh 986)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī of the Noble Lady, the Invincible One with the White Parasol, Who Emerged from the Crown of the Tathāgata, known in Sanskrit as the Āryatathāgatoṣṇīṣasitātapatrāparājitā nāma dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phags ma de bzhin gshegs pa'i gtsug tor nas byung ba'i gdugs dkar po can gzhan gyis mi thub pa zhes bya ba'i gzungs, is a dhāraṇī text centered on Sitātapatrā, the protective goddess of…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī of the Noble Mārīcī (Toh 988)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī of the Noble Marīcī, known in Sanskrit as Āryamārīcīnāmadhāraṇī and in Tibetan as 'Phags ma 'od zer can zhes bya ba'i gzungs, is a short scripture centered on Marīcī, a goddess whose name means "Ray of Light." It opens in the familiar style of a sūtra, with the Buddha staying at Jeta's Grove near Śrāvastī, surrounded by a great assembly of monks and bodhisattvas. There he tells the…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī of the Noble Goddess Cundā (Toh 989)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī of the Noble Goddess Cundā, known in Sanskrit as the Āryacundādevīnāmadhāraṇī and in Tibetan as 'Phags pa lha mo skul byed ma zhes bya ba'i gzungs, is a short dhāraṇī text devoted to the goddess Cundā. After paying homage to the Three Jewels and to the Buddha Vairocana, it praises Cundā as a powerful and wrathful protector, praised by all the tathāgatas, who overcomes adversaries and…

item.title: The Noble Vidyā-Mantra Called Jāṅgulī (Toh 990)
item.description: The Noble Vidyā-Mantra Called Jāṅgulī, known in Sanskrit as Āryajāṅgulīnāmavidyā and in Tibetan as Pakpa Dukselzhejawé Rikngak, whose Tibetan title literally means "the noble incantation called Dispeller of Poison," is a short scripture centered on a protective spell against poison and venomous snakes. It opens with the Buddha dwelling at Śrāvastī in Prince Jeta's Grove, where he tells the monks…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Endowed with Wealth (Toh 991)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Endowed with Wealth, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Hiraṇyaparī Nāma Dhāraṇī, is a short scripture centered on a dhāraṇī, a sacred formula believed to hold and convey spiritual power when it is retained and recited. Its setting is Tuṣita heaven, where the Blessed One sits on a stone slab white as wool among many thousands of bodhisattvas, each of whom has been prophesied…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī of Yaśovatī (Toh 992)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī of Yaśovatī, known in Sanskrit as the Āryayaśovatīdhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phags pa grags ldan ma'i gzungs, is a short ritual text devoted to protective and healing incantations. After paying homage to the Three Jewels and to the noble bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, it presents a series of mantras, each paired with simple instructions for its use. These include reciting a mantra…

item.title: The Queen of Vidyās Called the Blessed Lady (Toh 993)
item.description: The Queen of Vidyās Called the Blessed Lady, the Noble Aṅgulī, Accomplished by Recitation, known in Tibetan as Bklags pas 'grub pa bcom ldan 'das ma 'phags ma sor mo can, is a short protective scripture centered on a powerful female deity of mantra named Aṅgulī. Set on a mountain called King of Fragrance, where a community of monks is staying, it presents the noble Avalokiteśvara teaching a set…

item.title: The Noble Parṇaśabarī Sūtra (Toh 994)
item.description: The Noble Parṇaśabarī Sūtra, known in Sanskrit as the Āryaparṇaśabarīsūtra and in Tibetan as Phagpa Parnashawari Do, is a short protective text centered on Parṇaśabarī, a goddess traditionally associated with warding off epidemics and other dangers. It opens with homage to the Three Jewels, to the buddha Amitābha, and to the bodhisattvas Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta. It then gives an…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī of the Noble Parṇaśabarī (Toh 995)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī of the Noble Lady Parṇaśabarī, the Leaf-Clad Mountain Woman, known in Sanskrit as the Āryaparṇaśabarīdhāraṇī, is a short protective incantation addressed to the goddess Parṇaśabarī. Its Tibetan title describes her the same way, as the noble lady clad in leaves. The text opens with homages to the Three Jewels, to the Buddha Amitābha, and to the bodhisattvas Avalokiteśvara and…

item.title: The Noble Sūtra Called the Excellent Night (Toh 974)
item.description: The Noble Sūtra Called the Excellent Night, known in Sanskrit as the Āryabhadrarātrīnāmasūtra and in Tibetan as 'Phags pa mtshan mo bzang po zhes bya ba'i mdo, is a short discourse of the Buddha set at Rājagṛha, where the Blessed One is staying in the Bamboo Grove at the Kalandaka Feeding Ground. It opens with a radiant god who visits a monk at night on the bank of the Tapodā waters and asks…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Ocean of Dharma" (Toh 975)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Ocean of Dharma," known in Sanskrit as Ārya Dharmasāgara Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Pakpa Chökyi Gyatso Zhejawé Zung, is a short dhāraṇī scripture presented as the words of the Buddha himself. item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Refuge of Many Sons" (Toh 976)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Refuge of Many Sons," known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Bahuputra Pratisara Nāma Dhāraṇī, is a short scripture centered on a protective incantation taught by the Buddha. It opens at Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove of Anāthapiṇḍada's park, where the householder Anāthapiṇḍada comes to the Blessed One in distress, having quarreled bitterly with King Prasenajit and been driven away…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Certainty (Toh 977)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Certainty, known in Sanskrit as the Āryaniścayanāmadhāraṇī and in Tibetan as 'phags pa gdon mi za ba zhes bya ba'i gzungs, is a short dhāraṇī scripture in which the Buddha offers protection through the recitation of a spell. The teaching is set at Vaiśālī, in the Peaked Hall on the bank of the Markaṭa pond, where Śakra, lord of the gods, tells the Blessed One that he is…

item.title: The Great Invincible Knowledge Mantra (Toh 978)
item.description: The Great Knowledge Mantra That Cannot Be Overcome by Others, known in Sanskrit as Mahāvidyā Aparājita and in Tibetan as Gzhan gyis mi thub pa'i rig pa chen mo, is a brief protective text centered on a dhāraṇī, or incantation, of invincibility. After paying homage to the Buddha and to the seven buddhas of the past together with their communities of disciples, it invokes the distinctive virtues of…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī of the Rite of the Heart of Dependent Origination (Toh 979)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī of the Rite of the Heart of Dependent Origination, known in Sanskrit as the Āryapratītyasamutpādahṛdayavidhidhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Tenching Drelwar Jungwé Nyingpö Choga Zung, is a short ritual text built around the famous verse summarizing the Buddha's teaching on dependent origination. After paying homage to all buddhas and bodhisattvas, it recites the verse "Those…

item.title: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra Called Dependent Origination (Toh 980)
item.description: The Noble Great Vehicle Sūtra Called Dependent Origination, known in Sanskrit as the Āryapratītyasamutpādanāmamahāyānasūtra and in Tibetan as Phags pa rten cing 'brel bar 'byung ba zhes bya ba theg pa chen po'i mdo, is a brief Mahāyāna sūtra. It is set in the Heaven of the Thirty-Three, where the Buddha is joined by great śrāvakas such as Aśvajit, by bodhisattvas including Maitreya…

item.title: The Essence of Dependent Origination (Toh 981)
item.description: The Essence of Dependent Origination, known in Sanskrit as the Pratītyasamutpādahṛdaya and in Tibetan as Rten cing 'brel bar 'byung ba'i snying po, is a very brief text centered on the famous verse of dependent origination, which declares that the Tathāgata has taught the cause of phenomena that arise from causes, and also their cessation. After an opening homage to the buddhas, the text gives…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called the Pure Light of Stainless Rays (Toh 982)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called the Pure Light of Stainless Rays, known in Sanskrit as the Āryaraśmivimalaviśuddhaprabhā Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as 'Phags pa 'od zer dri ma med pa rnam par dag pa'i 'od ces bya ba'i gzungs, is a dhāraṇī scripture: a discourse built around a sacred incantation believed to carry purifying and protective power. item.title: The Dhāraṇī called "Light Rays Entering from Every Side, Shining with the Stainless Uṣṇīṣa, Beholding the Heart and the Pledge of All Tathāgatas" (Toh 983)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī called "Light Rays Entering from Every Side, Shining with the Stainless Uṣṇīṣa, Beholding the Heart and the Pledge of All Tathāgatas," known in Sanskrit as the Samantamukhapraveśaraśmivimaloṣṇīṣaprabhāsasarvatathāgatahṛdayasamayavilokita nāma dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Kun nas sgor 'jug pa'i 'od zer gtsug tor dri ma med par snang ba de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi snying po dang dam…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called the Victorious Uṣṇīṣa That Completely Purifies All Bad Destinies (Toh 984)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called the Victorious Uṣṇīṣa That Completely Purifies All Bad Destinies, known in Sanskrit as the Āryasarvadurgatipariśodhanī Uṣṇīṣavijayā Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Ngendro Tamche Yongsu Jongwa Tsuktor Nampar Gyalwa Zhejawai Zung, is a dhāraṇī scripture centered on the protective and purifying power of the Victorious Uṣṇīṣa incantation.
